es: Reconocer frases que permiten a otra persona salvar la cara tras un error o un comentario brusco, y expresar lamentos propios con wish e if only.

vocabulary.es: salvar las apariencias, no quedar en ridículo

teaching.en: It's easily done; I once sent a private message to the whole team, so this is only an honest mistake.
teaching.es: Es fácil que pase; una vez envié un mensaje privado a todo el equipo, así que esto es solo un error sin mala intención.
teaching.explanationEs: It's easily done quita peso al error: lo presenta como algo que le pasa a cualquiera, incluido el hablante.
segments: It's easily done; I once sent a private message to
the whole team, so this is only an honest mistake.
teaching.audioText: It's easily done; I once sent a private message to the whole team, so this is only an honest mistake.

teaching.en: I may not have been clear about the deadline, so I am happy to take the blame for the confusion.
teaching.es: Puede que yo no haya sido claro con el plazo, así que acepto con gusto la culpa de la confusión.
teaching.explanationEs: I may not have been clear reparte la culpa; take the blame = asumirla de forma voluntaria.
segments: I may not have been clear about the deadline, so
I am happy to take the blame for the confusion.
teaching.audioText: I may not have been clear about the deadline, so I am happy to take the blame for the confusion.

teaching.en: No real harm was done, so I will let you off the hook and we can avoid an awkward conversation.
teaching.es: No hubo ningún daño real, así que te libero de la culpa y podemos evitar una conversación incómoda.
teaching.explanationEs: No real harm resta importancia a las consecuencias; off the hook = libre de responsabilidad.
segments: No real harm was done, so I will let you
off the hook and we can avoid an awkward conversation.
teaching.audioText: No real harm was done, so I will let you off the hook and we can avoid an awkward conversation.

teaching.en: I should warn you that the remark sounded sharp, but I'll give you the benefit of the doubt.
teaching.es: Debo avisarte de que el comentario sonó áspero, pero te daré el beneficio de la duda.
teaching.explanationEs: El beneficio de la duda supone buena intención; I should warn you suaviza el aviso antes de la crítica.
segments: I should warn you that the remark sounded sharp,
but I'll give you the benefit of the doubt.
teaching.audioText: I should warn you that the remark sounded sharp, but I'll give you the benefit of the doubt.

teaching.en: In hindsight, I wish I had made the change clear in person; I hope there are no hard feelings.
teaching.es: Visto ahora, ojalá hubiera dejado clara la modificación en persona; espero que no haya rencores.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + had + participio lamenta algo pasado; in hindsight y no hard feelings suavizan el tono.
segments: In hindsight, I wish I had made the change clear
in person; I hope there are no hard feelings.
teaching.audioText: In hindsight, I wish I had made the change clear in person; I hope there are no hard feelings.

teaching.en: If only I had been clearer, the talk would not have been so awkward, and I could have helped you save face.
teaching.es: Si hubiera sido más claro, la charla no habría sido tan incómoda y te habría ayudado a salvar las apariencias.
teaching.explanationEs: If only + had + participio expresa un lamento sobre el pasado; save face = evitar que el otro quede mal.
segments: If only I had been clearer, the talk would not have
been so awkward, and I could have helped you save face.
teaching.audioText: If only I had been clearer, the talk would not have been so awkward, and I could have helped you save face.

prompt.es: Elige la frase de Sara que permite a Leo salvar la cara.

choices.text: You should have checked the attachment before you pressed send.
No harm done this time, but I will be checking everything you send from now on.
It's easily done; I nearly did the very same thing myself only last week.

feedback.es: Sara quita peso al error y se incluye a sí misma; las otras frases culpan a Leo con un reproche o con una amenaza disfrazada de consuelo.

hint.es: Busca la frase que normaliza el error sin acusar.

origin.text: Leo sent the client last year's price list by mistake and now sits red-faced at his desk. Sara, who saw the email go out, leans over and says something kind.

prompt.es: Completa: «No te preocupes: fue un error sin mala intención y no pasó nada grave.»

feedback.es: An honest mistake presenta el fallo como involuntario; eso ayuda al otro a salvar la cara.

hint.es: Sustantivo: un fallo involuntario; empieza por m.

origin.text: Don't worry about the late report. It was an honest ___, and no real harm was done.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puede que yo no haya sido claro con la hora.»

answer.text: I may not have been clear about the time

feedback.es: I may not have been clear reparte la culpa: el hablante asume parte del malentendido.

hint.es: Empieza por I may not have been y termina con about the time.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo ayuda la hablante a su compañera Mia.

choices.text: She hides the mistake from the manager in order to protect Mia.
She tells Mia off gently but promises to forgive her.
She insists that Mia explain herself to the manager.
She makes light of the mistake and shares responsibility for it.

feedback.es: La hablante quita peso («easily done») y reparte la culpa («I had not reminded her»); no esconde nada ni regaña.

origin.audio: Mia forgot to book the room, and the whole team arrived to find the door locked. I could have been angry, but I said it was easily done, that I had not reminded her, and that I would speak to the manager myself. She looked so relieved that we laughed about it over coffee.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el efecto que tiene sobre quien cometió el error.

pairs: It's easily done; it could happen to anyone
I may not have been clear about the start time
I'm sure you didn't mean it that way
No real harm done; we still have a week
I wish I had checked the room myself

feedback.es: Cada frase salva la cara de una manera: normaliza, reparte la culpa, supone buena intención, resta gravedad o lamenta algo propio.

pairs: It's easily done; it could happen to anyone

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto busca la autora con su respuesta a Tom?

choices.text: To reassure Tom and stop him feeling upset about the error.
To warn Tom that future errors will not be accepted.
To blame herself entirely and ask Tom to forgive her.
To point out that Tom should have checked the date twice.

feedback.es: Usa «easily done», comparte la culpa y resta importancia: tranquiliza a Tom, no le advierte, no se culpa por completo ni le reprocha.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for telling me straight away that you sent the invitation with the wrong date. It is easily done, and I suspect my original note was not clear either. I have corrected it, so no real harm has been done, and please do not apologise again.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué recurso usa Carlos para que Sara no pierda la cara.

choices.text: He takes the whole blame himself and apologises to the landlord.
He plays down the error and shares part of the responsibility.
He reminds her that the rent is late and must be paid today.
He warns her gently that the mistake could be very costly.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que es fácil que pase y que puede que él no fuera claro: quita peso y reparte la culpa, sin asumirla por entero ni advertir de costes.

origin.audio: Sara had promised to send the rent to the landlord by Friday, but on Monday she realised that she had used the wrong account number. She told Carlos, expecting him to be furious. Instead, he said it was easily done and added that he might not have been clear when he wrote the number on the fridge. He reminded her that the landlord had never charged a late fee, so no real harm was likely. Then he asked whether she wanted to ring the bank together. Sara said later that she felt lighter, although she still wished she had checked the number twice.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere el final del relato sobre cómo se siente Sara?

choices.text: Completely calm, since the matter is now closed.
Guilty, because Carlos ended up accepting most of the blame himself.
Relieved, although she still regrets her own mistake.
Worried, because the landlord may still refuse the payment.

feedback.es: Se siente más ligera, pero sigue deseando haber revisado el número: alivio con un resto de lamento propio.

origin.audio: Sara had promised to send the rent to the landlord by Friday, but on Monday she realised that she had used the wrong account number. She told Carlos, expecting him to be furious. Instead, he said it was easily done and added that he might not have been clear when he wrote the number on the fridge. He reminded her that the landlord had never charged a late fee, so no real harm was likely. Then he asked whether she wanted to ring the bank together. Sara said later that she felt lighter, although she still wished she had checked the number twice.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy dispuesta a darle el beneficio de la duda.»

feedback.es: The benefit of the doubt es la fórmula fija para suponer buena intención sin tener pruebas.

origin.text: Leo's comment about the presentation sounded rude. He was tired, though, and he has never been unkind before, so I am willing to give him the benefit of the ___.

prompt.es: Ayuda a Tom a salvar la cara: resta importancia y asume parte de la culpa.

answer.text: It's easily done, Tom, and no real harm has been done; I may not have been clear about the invoice code.
accepted: It's easily done, Tom, and no real harm has been done; I may not have been clear about the invoice code.
It could happen to anyone, Tom. I might not have been clear about the code on the invoice, so let's fix it together.

feedback.es: La respuesta combina dos recursos: normaliza el error (It's easily done) y reparte la culpa (I may not have been clear).

origin.text: Tom envió al cliente la factura equivocada. Dile que es fácil que pase y que quizá tú tampoco fuiste claro con el código de la factura.

evidenceGroups: i may not have been clear
i might not have been clear
i may not have made it clear

prompt.es: ¿Qué valora más la autora en este mensaje a Mia?

choices.text: That Mia had already fixed the notes before anyone noticed the gap.
That the new checklist will prevent every future error.
That she was right to remind Mia on Friday.
That Mia was honest about her slip instead of hiding it.

feedback.es: La autora dice preferir a una colega que admite un fallo antes que a una que lo oculta: valora la honestidad, no el control ni su propio aviso.

origin.text: Hi Mia, thanks for telling me about the missing notes. I'm sure you didn't mean to leave them out, and honestly, I should have reminded you on Friday. In hindsight, the plan was vague, so let's agree on a checklist and move on. No hard feelings at all; I would rather have a colleague who admits a slip than one who hides it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No pasó nada grave y podemos seguir adelante.»

answer.text: No real harm was done and we can move on

feedback.es: No real harm was done resta importancia y and we can move on cierra el asunto sin reproches.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es amable dejarlo libre de culpa y seguir adelante.»

feedback.es: Let someone off the hook es la expresión para librar a alguien de la culpa; take o get him off the hook también existen.

origin.text: Everyone makes mistakes at work. When a colleague slips, it is kind to ___ him off the hook and simply move on.
